trigger: Breach of unsecured PHI (presumed unless the 164.402 four-factor assessment shows a low probability of compromise). Clock starts at discovery: the first day known, or by reasonable diligence would have been known, to any workforce member (164.404(a)(2))
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery
notify: Each affected individual by first-class mail (or email if the individual agreed); substitute notice if contact information is insufficient or out of date (164.404(d)(2))

obligation: HIPAA breach notice to HHS (500 or more)
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals (likely here: a full trip-list export covers up to about 5,200 patients)
deadline: Contemporaneously with the individual notices (within 60 days of discovery)
notify: HHS Secretary through the OCR breach portal

obligation: HIPAA breach log to HHS (fewer than 500)
deadline: No later than 60 days after the end of the calendar year in which the breach was discovered
notify: HHS Secretary through the OCR breach portal

trigger: Breach affecting more than 500 residents of a state or jurisdiction
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery
notify: Prominent media outlets serving Florida (or the affected area)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if more than 500 Florida residents

trigger: A law enforcement official states that notice would impede a criminal investigation
deadline: Delay for the period in a written statement; if oral, document it and delay no longer than 30 days unless a written statement follows
notify: Hold HIPAA notices; document the request

obligation: Business associate breach notice to the company (inbound; platform vendor, MSP, phone vendor, billing company)
trigger: A business associate discovers a breach of the company's unsecured PHI
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after the BA's discovery (BAAs may set shorter periods)
notify: The company (Office Manager as Privacy Officer)

trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents (includes medical history, condition, treatment, or diagnosis, and health insurance policy or subscriber numbers). Clock starts at determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination (15 more days if good cause is given to the department in writing within the 30 days, per 501.171(3)(a)). Notice under the HIPAA rules is deemed compliant with this subsection if the company follows those rules (501.171(4)(g))
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - plan to the 30-day date; counsel confirms the deemed-compliance path

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination (the 15-day good-cause extension in 501.171(3)(a) applies only to notice to individuals). A company that timely sends the Department a copy of its HIPAA notice is deemed compliant with subsection (3)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Florida residents

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies (timing, distribution, and content of the notices)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if more than 1,000 (likely for a full trip-list export)

trigger: A law enforcement agency determines individual notice would interfere with a criminal investigation
deadline: Delay on the agency's written request for the period it specifies
notify: Hold Florida individual notices; keep the written request

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice to the company (inbound)
trigger: Breach of a system maintained by a third-party agent (for example the platform vendor, the MSP, or the billing company)
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 10 days after the agent's determination
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - add to vendor contracts at renewal

trigger: Affected patients who reside outside Florida (for example seasonal residents transported to dialysis)
notify: Residents and regulators under each state's law

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement (FBI) or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI through IC3 or CISA

deadline: As soon as practicable (voluntary; supports the OFAC mitigating factor)
notify: FBI field office or IC3; CISA

trigger: Suspected security incident, extortion demand, or data theft
deadline: Per policy: prompt notice through the 24x7 breach hotline, before hiring outside firms; use panel counsel and forensics

citation: Transport agreement with the regional hospital (contract)
trigger: Security incident that may affect the hospital's patients or the company's ability to provide booked transports
notify: Hospital contract manager and privacy office

obligation: CIRCIA incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident (reasonable belief) or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after a ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25 (voluntary until then). The company is under the SBA size standard, and it is unclear whether a non-emergency-only transport company would meet the proposed EMS criterion (population of 50,000 or more). Recheck when final

deadline: Immediately, and no more than 1 hour after discovery
notify: Organizational incident handlers; CSO, SIB Chief or Interface Agency Official; FBI CJIS ISO
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company has no access to criminal justice information (P03 section 1)

trigger: Contractor identifies covered equipment or a Kaspersky covered article
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification for covered telecommunications equipment or services (52.204-25(d)); within 3 business days for a Kaspersky covered article (52.204-23(c)); further report within 10 business days in both cases
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts (Medicare billing is not a procurement contract)
